points.description: States all three items to be learned: centers, weights and biases (all three named).
points.partial_credit: Two of the three items named correctly and none wrong earns half.

points.description: Difference to other NNs: RBFN has a single hidden layer with a linear output layer, whereas a general NN can have multiple hidden layers and a linear or non-linear output layer.
points.partial_credit: Only one side stated precisely (RBFN single hidden layer + linear output, or NN multiple hidden layers/non-linear output) earns half.

points.description: Pros: states that RBFN is a universal approximator and that it is easy to add more centers.
points.partial_credit: One of the two pros stated precisely earns half.

points.description: Con: states that the bias is not unique.

rubric.notes: Full marks need every element stated explicitly with the correct terms (centers, weights, biases; single hidden layer; linear output layer; universal approximator; bias not unique). Vague or generic statements earn nothing for that point, and a wrong statement or wrong extra item in a point cancels it. Part marks only where the partial_credit condition is clearly met; total is capped at 2.
